alerts.reason: TreeHouse net sales fell 3.9% (A), just 1.1 percentage points from the threshold. B identifies planned distribution exits in coffee and in-store bakery. Further volume losses from those exits could push the decline to 5% within two quarters.

Boston Beer returned to 3.9% revenue growth (A), but shipments rose only 0.9% as Truly and other brands declined (B). Shipments exceeded depletions ahead of peak season (C). If wholesalers draw down inventory, orders could fall enough for revenue to cross back to -5%.

Intel's Q1 revenue grew 8.6%, helped by a PC inventory comparison that favored Q1 (A, B). Server volumes fell (C), and 5G, Altera and Mobileye customers cut purchases to reduce inventories (D, E). If those cuts persist as the PC comparison fades, consolidated revenue could fall 5% year on year in Q2 or Q3.

Norfolk Southern's revenue decline narrowed from 5.07% to 4.09%, placing it back above the threshold. B says higher volumes partly offset lower pricing, fuel surcharges and storage revenue. A slightly smaller volume gain could let those pressures take revenue growth back to -5% within two quarters.
